data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for 15-year-olds in Chinese Taipei using the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking test. The test measures three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Chinese Taipei’s mean creative thinking score is 33 on a 60-point scale, which is on par with the OECD average. The factsheet reports proficiency distribution (78% at Level 3 or above; 27% at Level 5 or 6) and relative strengths by ideation process and domain context, including higher relative performance in tasks requiring generating creative ideas and written expression. It also reports associations with mathematics and reading performance (correlations of 0.68 and 0.67, respectively) and socio-economic and gender gaps, but it does not provide an ML modeling pipeline or PV/missing-data handling details in the excerpt.
